title: Last feature loop results
first_prompt: Summarize results of the last feature loop

commits.summary: jvmcontract and build.py: a counterexample keeps its witness as typed data, enough to rebuild the call (verification pending)
commits.body:
Second half of step 3b of llm-dlc/loops/build-orchestration.md. In lib/, a counterexample from equivalence and prove keeps its witness as data next to its text (witness::Typed, witness::Call): the checker's inputs under the harness's names with their Java types and exact values (long as a decimal string, float/double as Java's toString, char as its code unit, arrays element by element), the inputs before shrinking, the patched version's call (class, class file, method, descriptor, static or not, receiver as a record of its components, each argument naming the input it comes from), and for regression proofs the previous version's call, where an argument under --before-arguments names the expression that computed it and a receiver built by new R(...) is a record of those values. build.py records it as counterexamples[].witness and properties[].counterexample, with each call's classFileSha256 from the classes the run built; the schema gains typedValue, typedCall and witness. Only fields were added: interpreter and JBMC results committed for existing examples are untouched.

Verified: cargo test (118 unit, 50 integration; new assertions for a record receiver against a static previous version, a previous receiver built by an expression, the same record in both versions, a char witness and a native long witness), test_build.py 107 tests, test_pipeline.py 20 tests, no page moved under --render-only. The Java version string 25.0.4.1 that the tool identities record was read as a public IP by the redactor; the user approved it as a false positive in a separate commit.

commits.summary: build.py: a page says whether its result is still the current files' result, and an explanation is the reason only for the expected verdict (verification pending)
commits.body:
Step 3c of llm-dlc/loops/build-orchestration.md. snapshot() classifies a recorded result as current, stale (with what changed) or unknown (recorded before claims existed), and lists evidence files that are not the run's bundle. claim_changes() fingerprints the claim again from the current files: the plan's statement, the scope (claim_scope(), now shared with claim_record()), the patch and the sources the patch applies to. The patched sources and models are those sources with the patch applied, so nothing is copied or patched. A stale page leads with a warning naming what changed; the router's verdict cell says (⚠ stale), index.json records snapshot, and --render-only prints NNN-name: stale (why). Rendering rewrites no result. 'Why the verdict is right' holds the author's explanation only when the run gave the expected result; otherwise the section is 'What the example expected', naming both results and quoting the explanation as the expected one's.

Every page moved by one line under Evidence: all 140 recorded results predate claims, so they render as unknown. No recorded result misses its expectation, so no explanation section moved. A full --render-only takes 2.6 s. Verified: test_build.py 115 tests (new SnapshotTest: current, stale by patch, scope, statement, sources with build output left out, and claim format; evidence not the bundle; unknown; --render-only showing a stale fixture in the page, router row and index.json without rewriting the result; the explanation for missed, unevaluable and older results), test_pipeline.py 20 tests.

commits.summary: build.py: every command is a logged stage, and a pipeline job keeps each attempt's workspace (verification pending)
commits.body:
Step 3d of llm-dlc/loops/build-orchestration.md, which completes Phase 3. Every command build.py makes goes through stage(name, command). Inside an attempt, its stdout and stderr stream into logs/NN-name.stdout/.stderr as it runs, and logs/stages.jsonl gets a line as each stage starts and ends. A path-free progress line is printed for each, and the attempt records stages (name, exited/killed/timed-out/not-started, exit code, seconds, log paths). A timeout raises with the output so far. In a pipeline job the scratch directory sits under $VERIFY_WORKDIR/.build-py and is never removed, so each attempt keeps its patched copy (harnesses, the tools' work directories), logs and evidence, named by attempt.workspace; the pipeline keeps that work directory for a job that does not pass and collects only declared outputs. Outside the pipeline each copy is removed when its run ends, as before. The unpatched baseline of a regression proof no longer compiles tests.

Measured first: an app copies in 0.01-0.05 s and compiles main in 0.56-0.73 s and tests in 0.56-0.72 s (Quorum, Crosscut, Mica), so a cross-job baseline cache would save under a second per job and is not added; Box Office's Gradle builds will be timed by attempt.stages from the jobs below. Checked and not needed: git apply inside a repository's tree patches the copy as in /tmp, since it prefixes the patch's paths with its directory; a test covers it. Verified: test_build.py 123 tests (new StagesTest: streamed logs and records, check, a timeout keeping partial output, a killed stage, capture outside an attempt, an interrupted run leaving claim.json, the copy and every stage's log in the kept workspace, a pipeline attempt's stages and workspace, the copy removed outside the pipeline, the baseline compiled without tests), test_pipeline.py 20 tests, no page moved under --render-only.
